body.p: In the Office Action, claims 1, 5, 12, and 15 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as being anticipated by Starke et al. (US 6,016,016). Claims 2-4 and 13-14 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke in view of Sharma (US 2017/0066534). Claims 6, 9 and 11 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke in view of Mattes et al. (US 2004/0048582). Claim 7 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke in view of Mattes and Sharma. Claim 8 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke in view of Mattes and Klose et al. (US 2018/079507). Claim 10 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Starke in view of Mattes and Francois et al. (US 8,321,611). Applicant respectfully traverses the foregoing rejections and requests reconsideration.

Notwithstanding the foregoing traversal, solely in an effort to expedite prosecution, Applicant had amended claim 1 to recite "a multiplicity of sensors which collect passenger-based sensor data" and "wherein the electrical energy supply system has a sensor data processing device accommodated within the first electronics housing which is designed to preprocess the passenger-based sensor data." These amendments are fully supported and add no new matter. See Published Application 0047-48. Claim 12 has been similarly amended.

As noted in Applicant's Specification, the features of claims 1 and 12 make "it possible to control different sensors, the sensor data from which are acquired intermittently or continuously and preprocessed locally in the electrical energy supply device. The passenger-based sensor data preprocessed in this manner can then be augmented with further aircraft-based or environment-based data and centrally evaluated." See Published Application 0010. Also, a "sensor data processing device 5a is arranged in the first electronics housing 5 and is designed to preprocess the sensor data acquired from the sensors 1, 2, 3 and/or 4." Published Application 0044. The sensor data processing device improves the processing efficiency of the passenger seat arrangement by allowing local preprocessing of the passenger-based sensor data.

The cited references fail to disclose or suggest the features of claims 1 and 12. Starke discloses "a passenger seat 12 with a voltage supply apparatus for operating electric devices of a passenger is represented." Starke Col. 4, lines 6-8. The passenger seat 12 includes a socket 22 in the left armrest 24 of the passenger seat 12 which is connected to a power supply device 16 via a signal line 18 and a double-wire supply line 20. See Starke Col. 4, lines 10-15.

The socket 22 includes an optical infrared reflection sensor 48 arranged as a casing detector, such that "the reflection sensor 48 can detect if a plug casing 51 is present at the socket 22." See Starke Col. 4, lines 46-56. Therefore, the reflection sensor 48 simply detects whether a plug casing 51 is inserted into the socket 22. As such, Starke fails to disclose or suggest a multiplicity of sensors which collect passenger-based sensor data and fails to disclose or suggest a sensor data processing device accommodated within the first electronics housing which is designed to preprocess the passenger-based sensor data.

Accordingly, even if combined, a point Applicant does not concede, the resulting combination of the cited references fails to disclose or suggest all of the features of claims 1 and 12. Thus, claims 1 and 12 should be allowable over the cited art. Those claims that depend therefrom should be allowable as well-at least by virtue of their claim dependency.

Applicant has added new claims 16-18 which are fully supported and add no new matter. See Published Application 0037, 0043, and 0047. Applicant respectfully submits that claims 16-18 are allowable over the cited references-at least by virtue of their claim dependency.

Applicant therefore respectfully submits that all of the claims of the application should be found to be allowable and thus requests that the Examiner indicate all of the claims as allowed and pass the application to allowance.

The amendments to the claims were done merely to expedite prosecution of the present case. Applicant reserves any and all rights to pursue the subject matter of the original claims in this application, or in another application. Moreover, these amendments should not be construed as an admission or acquiescence to any rejection.

Furthermore, the fact that Applicant has only addressed certain rejections should not be considered to be acquiescence to the rejections. Rather, Applicant has presented the argument herein in an effort to expedite prosecution. Applicant reserves any and all rights to address any rejection made but not specifically addressed herein.
